stem: Nitin starts at point P facing South. He walks 5 m South, then turns right and walks 12 m. He then turns right again and walks 5 m. What is the straight-line distance from P to Nitin's current position?

per_option_rationale.rationale: South 5 m, right turn to West, West 12 m, right turn to North, North 5 m. The two 5 m legs cancel. Net displacement = 12 m West from P.
Student adds all three leg lengths (5+12+5=22) to get the path length, not the straight-line distance from P.
Student ignores the third 5 m leg and treats the endpoint as (12 m West, 5 m South), giving sqrt(144+25)=13 via the 5-12-13 triple.
Student adds only the first and second leg lengths (5+12=17), treating the path as a straight two-leg sum without any geometry.

explanation: Starting at P facing South: walk 5 m to (0,-5). Turn right (now West): walk 12 m to (-12,-5). Turn right (now North): walk 5 m to (-12,0). The North and South legs cancel (5 m South then 5 m North). The net position is 12 m due West of P. Distance = 12 m.

explanation_sections.punchline: Lock the direction chain first: South, right turn = West, right turn = North. That is the cracking move - it reveals that leg 1 (5 m South) and leg 3 (5 m North) are on the same axis in opposite directions and cancel. Net displacement = 12 m West. Distance = 12 m.
explanation_sections.approach: Step 1 (track directions): Start facing South. Right turn from South = West (walk 12 m). Right turn from West = North (walk 5 m). Step 2 (assign vectors): South 5 m = (0, -5). West 12 m = (-12, 0). North 5 m = (0, +5). Step 3 (sum components): x-total = -12, y-total = -5 + 5 = 0. Step 4 (distance): sqrt((-12)^2 + 0^2) = 12 m. Verify: do the two 5 m legs cancel? Yes - South and North are opposite. No Pythagorean computation needed. This vector-sum recipe applies to any multi-leg displacement problem.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always sum displacement components separately on each axis before reaching for a Pythagorean calculation. Opposite-direction legs on the same axis cancel to zero. The 5-12-13 trap (option 3) comes from ignoring the third leg entirely.
explanation_sections.timing: About 90 seconds. Tracking two right turns from South: 20 seconds. Writing three displacement vectors: 20 seconds. Summing components and checking cancellation: 20 seconds. sqrt(144): 10 seconds. Trap: option 3 (13 m) uses the 5-12-13 Pythagorean triple - it assumes you stop after the second leg. Always complete all legs before computing.
